items: ## 8\. Further Study Options After a Master’s in Mechanical Engineering
After completing a relevant master’s degree, students may explore additional qualifications or research opportunities in areas such as:
PhD in Mechanical Engineering: Research into mechanics, materials, design or engineering systems.
PhD in Energy Engineering: Research into energy efficiency, sustainable technologies and thermal systems.
Master’s in Automotive Engineering: Specialisation in vehicle design, powertrains and automotive systems.
Master’s in Manufacturing Engineering: Advanced production systems, manufacturing processes and industrial optimisation.
Master’s in Robotics and Mechatronics: Study of automation, robotics, control systems and integrated mechanical-electronic systems.
Master’s in Renewable Energy: Advanced study of sustainable power generation and energy technologies.
These are possible study directions, not a list of confirmed programmes available in Mauritius. Admission depends on the institution, previous qualification and subject prerequisites.
## 9\. Career Opportunities After Mechanical Engineering

A recognised postgraduate engineering qualification can support careers across industrial, manufacturing, energy and technical sectors. Opportunities depend on the degree, practical experience and the requirements of individual employers. For students considering a Master’s in Mechanical Engineering in Mauritius for Indian Students, the course curriculum and practical training should be evaluated alongside potential career paths.
Potential career paths include:
Mechanical design engineer: Designs and evaluates mechanical components and systems.
Manufacturing engineer: Improves production processes, equipment and efficiency.
Thermal systems engineer: Works with heating, cooling, heat transfer and thermal equipment.
Energy engineer: Supports energy efficiency and energy-system projects.
Building services engineer: Works with mechanical systems such as ventilation, heating and cooling in buildings.
Quality engineer: Helps improve product quality and manufacturing processes.
Project engineer: Coordinates engineering projects, technical tasks and delivery.
Research and development engineer: Supports the design, testing and improvement of products and systems.

A related postgraduate qualification may support these career directions, but specialised engineering roles can require specific technical experience, professional registration or additional training.

## 11\. Frequently Asked Questions
### 1\. Is a Master’s in Mechanical Engineering available in Mauritius?

A dedicated Master’s in Mechanical Engineering was not found in the University of Mauritius’s published postgraduate programme list for 2026–2027. Related options include Building Services Engineering and Sustainable Energy Engineering with Environmental Management.
### 2\. Which university offers related postgraduate engineering courses?

The University of Mauritius lists postgraduate programmes in Building Services Engineering, Sustainable Energy Engineering with Environmental Management, Renewable Energy and Smart Electrical Systems, and other engineering-related areas. Contact the university to confirm which options fit your academic background.
### 3\. What is the cost of studying Mechanical Engineering in Mauritius?

A verified tuition fee for a dedicated Mechanical Engineering master’s is not available because the programme has not been confirmed. Indicative living expenses are estimated at MUR 15,000–25,000 per month, or approximately ₹28,500–₹47,500 using the illustrative exchange rate in this article. Tuition and other expenses are additional.
### 4\. What qualifications are required for postgraduate engineering study?

Applicants generally need a recognised bachelor’s degree in an appropriate discipline and must meet the programme’s academic requirements. The specific subject background and grades required depend on the chosen course.
### 5\. What careers can I pursue after a Mechanical Engineering master’s?

Depending on your qualification and experience, potential careers include mechanical design engineer, manufacturing engineer, energy engineer, building services engineer, quality engineer and research and development engineer.
